Semantic clustering of gastruloid publications

Source: vignettes/gastruloid_paper_clustering.qmd

1 Overview

For ~30 gastruloid papers, citation graphs alone poorly separate experimental protocol from biological findings. Free browsers (?@tbl-nocode-tools) help exploration; a section-aware dual-view pipeline (Figure 1) is better for a review-quality taxonomy (Singh et al. 2023; AllenAI 2023).

Represent each paper with two views (protocol vs insight), not one fused embedding early on:

\[\mathbf{z}_i^{\mathrm{prot}},\; \mathbf{z}_i^{\mathrm{ins}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d} \tag{1}\]

Similarity is cosine on each view separately:

\[S_{ij}^{(v)} = \frac{ \langle \mathbf{z}_i^{(v)}, \mathbf{z}_j^{(v)} \rangle }{ \|\mathbf{z}_i^{(v)}\|_2\,\|\mathbf{z}_j^{(v)}\|_2 } ,\qquad v \in \{\mathrm{prot},\mathrm{ins}\} \tag{2}\]

2 Decision: no-code vs full pipeline

2.1 No-code path

Free no-code tools for a small gastruloid corpus
Tool Free Signal Role here
Citrus Search (Citrus Search 2024) ✓ Content embeddings Best no-code match for protocol/content grouping
Inciteful (Inciteful 2024) ✓ Citations + similarity Landmark neighbourhoods; missing papers
Connected Papers (Connected Papers 2024) Limited Citation graph Visual splits (species, tissue, signalling)

Prefer Citrus for content/protocol likeness and Inciteful for citation neighbourhoods; treat Connected Papers as an optional visual check (Citrus Search 2024; Inciteful 2024; Connected Papers 2024).

2.2 Full pipeline (summarised)

2.2.1 a. Paper extraction — GROBID

Parse PDFs to scholarly TEI/XML (title, abstract, sections, references) (GROBID contributors 2024). Normalise headings to methods, results, discussion, captions; exclude the reference list from clustering features.

2.2.2 b. Feature engineering — protocol vs insights

Do not fuse views yet. Build:

  • Protocol text — methods (+ captions / supplementary methods when present)
  • Insight text — results + discussion (+ abstract/conclusion)

Optionally fill a short schema (species, aggregate size, CHIR/RA timing, assays, main phenotype) to support later filtering; classic gastruloid axes include mESC aggregates and WNT/CHIR timing (Brink et al. 2014).

2.2.3 c. Ontology matching — scispaCy

Run biomedical NER (scispaCy; optionally PubTator3) and map entities to MeSH / GO (AllenAI 2024; NCBI 2024; NLM 2024; Gene Ontology Consortium 2024). Store as sparse flags or TF–IDF over ontology IDs to stabilise synonym variants (e.g. CHIR / CHIR99021).

2.2.4 d. Embeddings — free scientific models

Use non-commercial scientific encoders: SPECTER2 (title+abstract paper anchor) and/or SciBERT (section/chunk encoding) (AllenAI 2023; Beltagy et al. 2019; Singh et al. 2023). Pool chunk embeddings into \(\mathbf{z}^{\mathrm{prot}}\) and \(\mathbf{z}^{\mathrm{ins}}\) (Equation 1); L2-normalise for cosine (Equation 2).

2.2.5 e. Similarity matrices

Compute exact cosine matrices \(S^{(\mathrm{prot})}\) and \(S^{(\mathrm{ins})}\) (Equation 2). With ~30 papers, ANN indices are unnecessary.

2.2.6 f. Clustering — hierarchical or modular

Prefer hierarchical structure or module-based partitions:

  • agglomerative clustering (average linkage on cosine) + dendrogram; or
  • HDBSCAN for hierarchical density clusters with outliers (McInnes et al. 2017); or
  • Leiden on a \(k\)-NN similarity graph for modular communities (Traag et al. 2019).

Run protocol and insight spaces separately, then cross-tabulate cluster memberships (?@tbl-outputs).

2.2.7 h. Cluster labelling — BERTopic

Label clusters with BERTopic / c-TF-IDF terms grounded in member sections (Grootendorst 2022), e.g. mouse mESC · CHIR-pulse · axial organisation.

2.2.8 i. Visualisation — NetworkX or Neo4j

Export papers as nodes and high-similarity edges as a graph in NetworkX (local) or Neo4j (queryable) (NetworkX developers 2024; Neo4j 2024). Optionally project embeddings with UMAP for a 2D map (McInnes et al. 2018) — plots support interpretation, they are not the clustering itself.

2.2.9 j. Mathematical validation

Report intrinsic metrics (silhouette, Davies–Bouldin, Calinski–Harabasz) on each view (Rousseeuw 1987). With a small expert-labelled pair set, add ARI/NMI and Precision@k for nearest neighbours. Case-check that known families (mouse/CHIR/axial; human RA/Matrigel posterior; tissue-specialised outputs) reappear (Brink et al. 2014).

Linked outputs from the dual-view clustering design
Output Content
Protocol clusters Families of induction / culture / perturbation pipelines
Insight clusters Families of biological claims and phenotypes
Protocol × insight cross-tab Same method, different claims (or the reverse)

3 Python modules (pipeline roles)

Python and related tooling mentioned in the full pipeline
Module / tool Role in the pipeline
grobid (service) PDF → structured TEI sections (GROBID contributors 2024)
scispacy Biomedical NER / sentence processing (AllenAI 2024)
PubTator3 API Concept annotation & relations (NCBI 2024)
transformers + SciBERT / SPECTER2 Free scientific embeddings (Beltagy et al. 2019; AllenAI 2023)
sentence-transformers Convenient pooling / cosine helpers (Reimers and Gurevych 2019)
numpy / scipy Similarity matrices (Equation 2)
hdbscan Hierarchical density clustering (McInnes et al. 2017)
leidenalg / igraph Modular graph clustering (Traag et al. 2019)
bertopic Cluster topic labels (Grootendorst 2022)
networkx Local similarity graphs (NetworkX developers 2024)
neo4j (optional) Persist/query paper networks (Neo4j 2024)
umap-learn 2D visualisation of embeddings (McInnes et al. 2018)
scikit-learn Agglomerative clustering; silhouette & related metrics (Rousseeuw 1987)

4 Recommendation

Start with ?@tbl-nocode-tools if the goal is orientation. For a publication-quality gastruloid map, follow Figure 1 (full branch): GROBID → dual protocol/insight features → ontology terms → SciBERT/SPECTER2 → cosine \(S\) → hierarchical/modular clustering → BERTopic labels → NetworkX/Neo4j → intrinsic validation (Equation 1; Equation 2; ?@tbl-outputs; ?@tbl-python-modules).
